input.add_to_description: Day 5 dusk at the ford: appears in person, silver-haired, fifties, clove-and-ink scent, warm voice. Came alone onto the stones at Wren's call, Garrow held at the bank. Wren's Insight (22): his warmth is real AND practiced; he is afraid, not of Wren but of what Elowen's coffer holds; his hands shake slightly; he did not expect the coffer to be opened. He has not yet said what became of Elowen.

entries.text:
You take the flat stone mid-ford with the river chattering around it, psalter under your arm, pendant catching the last copper light. When the wagon creaks to a halt on the bank, you call across the water, and your Performance check, a 16, carries every word to Hob's door and the villagers on the shore. Murmurs stop.

For a long moment nothing moves. Garrow's hand drifts to his coat, and Corvin lays two fingers on his sleeve without looking at him. Garrow stops.

Then the driver's box creaks and Corvin Tallowmere climbs down. Silver-haired, straight-backed, in a plain travelling coat, smelling even from here of cloves and ink. He walks to the water and, alone, steps onto the stones. He crosses them with the easy balance you remember from a hundred river crossings, and stops one stone short of yours.

"Wren," he says, warm as ever. "You've grown into your voice."

Your Insight check was a 22, and it's clear. The warmth is real and practised both, as it always was. But his hands are not steady, and his eyes keep dropping to the pendant at your throat and the psalter under your arm. He isn't afraid of you. He's afraid of what you've opened. He didn't expect the coffer to give.

"I see you've been to the spur," he says quietly. "Then you've read her letter. I would ask you not to judge me before I say what became of Elowen." He glances at the shore, at Hob, at the watchers. "But not in front of a village. Walk with me three stones, and I'll tell you, or I'll tell you here if you insist."

The water slides cold around the stones. Alder and Kit are in the willows, Hob is on his step, and Garrow waits on the bank. The sun is almost down.

What does Wren do?

input.add_to_description: Day 5 ~5:10 PM: arrived at the ford with the wagon, Garrow and the driver. Obeyed Wren's call to come alone to the mid-ford stone; sent Garrow to wait on the bank. Silver-haired, warm-voiced, in a long green-grey coat, walking stick in hand. His eyes went straight to the silver lantern pendant at Wren's throat and for an instant his charm slipped.

entries.text:
The ford is loud around the flat stone, the water chattering over the weir below you. You stand on it with your hands empty, the pendant bright at your throat and the psalter under your arm. On the bank a few villagers hold their breath. Hob's pipe has stopped smoking. Somewhere in the willows, Alder and Kit are very still.

The wagon creaks to a halt at the water's edge, its painted lantern swinging. Garrow stops at the lead horse's head. His easy smile is gone, and he looks at you the way a man looks at a bad debt. The driver stays on the box. Then a figure climbs down from the tailboard, and your stomach tightens before you've admitted who it is.

Corvin Tallowmere is as you left him. He is silver-haired and warm-faced, in a long green-grey coat, with a walking stick he doesn't need. He lifts a hand to Garrow without looking at him. "Stay with the horses, Garrow. The girl asks it, and she's quite right to." His voice carries over the water, easy and fond, the voice that sold a hundred noble houses their ancestors.

He steps onto the first stone, then the second, picking his way across like a man crossing his own hall. Halfway he stops. His eyes have found the silver lantern at your throat, and for one bare heartbeat the charm falls off his face, and what's under it is neither warm nor angry. It looks like fear, and something older than fear. Then the smile is back.

"You've been to the spur," he says softly, and comes the last few stones to stand an arm's length from you, with the river running between his boots. "Well, my girl. You've been a good deal busier than I guessed. Shall we talk like family, then, or shall we talk like the truth?"

His stick rests on the stone, and Garrow waits on the bank. The village watches. What does Wren say?

input.add_to_description: Day 5 dusk: arrives at the ford by wagon with Garrow and the driver. Wren's call (7) did not sway him; he answers lightly and amused, does not leave Garrow behind, but does step down and walks toward the stones. Description: tall, silver-haired, clove-scented, warm voice, a lantern-headed cane.

entries.text:
You stand on the flat stone with the water chattering past your boots, the psalter under your arm and the pendant catching the last copper light. You call across the ford, clear and level. Your roll was a 7, and it doesn't land the way you hoped.

The wagon creaks to a halt on the far bank. The driver stays on the box. Garrow stops at the lead horse's head, smiling his thin smile. Then the canvas flap lifts and Corvin Tallowmere steps down.

He is exactly as you remember him: tall and silver-haired, in a good dark coat, a clove-and-ink scent drifting over the water, a lantern-headed cane in his hand. He looks at you across the stream with such open fondness that your stomach turns.

"Leave Garrow?" he calls, amused, his voice warm and carrying the way you were taught to carry yours. "My girl, a man doesn't walk into a river to meet a cat with a knife in her sleeve unprotected. But I'll not make you shout." He nods, and Garrow doesn't move, but doesn't step back either. Corvin starts across the stepping stones alone, unhurried, his cane tapping each one. On the bank behind you Hob has stopped smoking, and villagers are edging down to the water. In the willows, something rustles faintly. That will be Alder and Kit.

He stops two stones away, close enough to talk without raising his voice. His eyes go to the psalter, then the pendant at your throat, and for the first time his smile falters.

"You found the coffer," he says softly. "Of course you did."

The ford is between you, the crowd is listening, and Garrow is thirty paces behind him. What does Wren say or do?

input.add_to_description: Day 5 dusk at the ford: came on foot, alone, unarmed save a belt-knife, leaving Garrow on the bank. Wren's natural-20 Insight: his eyes went to the silver pendant, not the psalter; his fear is real; his guilt is that of a man who ran from something, not one who killed. He wears Elowen's iron decoy key on a cord. He knows where Elowen went and has not said.

entries.text:
The stones are cold and wet under your boots. You stand on the flat one mid-ford with the river chattering around it, the psalter under your arm and the pendant catching the last copper light. On the bank Hob puffs his pipe and a knot of villagers watches. Alder and Kit are somewhere in the willows.

The wagon halts at the water's edge, its painted lantern swinging. Garrow stops beside the lead horse, smile pinned in place. At your call he glances at the wagon. A figure climbs down from the box, and Garrow stays where he is.

Corvin comes alone, picking his way over the stepping stones in his good grey cloak, belt-knife the only weapon you can see. He is thinner than you remember, and older.

Your Insight check was a natural 20, so you see more than you meant to. His eyes go to the silver pendant at your throat, not the psalter, and they stay there. His hands are not quite steady. Beneath the charm his fear is real, but it isn't the fear of a man who has lost money. It's the fear of someone who ran from something once and has been running ever since. Whatever he did to Elowen, you'd stake your life it wasn't murder. There's an iron key on a cord at his neck, the decoy that never fit.

He stops two stones short and spreads his empty hands, with the old warm smile gone thin. "Wren," he says. "You look like her. I hoped you wouldn't." His voice drops so only you can hear. "You opened the coffer. Then you know what I am. Ask me what you came to ask."

The light is going. The villagers are watching, and Garrow is waiting. What does Wren say or do?

While near your temple, you can call upon the priests for assistance, provided the assistance you ask for is not hazardous and you remain in good standing with your temple.

spellcasting.notes: Spells known are fixed until a level-up.
